head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Plan independent registered verifier construction and verification as separate simultaneous-storage phases before allocating the trusted empty machine shape.
Bound cap backing capacity at 64 KiB and account for shape, common-data containers, symbolic workspace, retained lookup metadata, one admitted proof and verification scratch.
Admit caller proof backing before independent metadata construction in recursive Registry::verify; capacity checks remain separate from envelope and numerical verification.
Add the 257 MiB verifier component once per serial worker to matching Rust and Python witness host reservations.
Correct stale resource-test host budgets and fake GPU assignment versions; preserve both failed qualification attempts and validate the final source across GPU and CPU builds.
limitations: This bounds one independent native registered verifier component, not complete worker RSS. Caller caches, registry/result containers, stacks, callbacks and allocator/driver/OS overhead need enclosing admission.
Caller proof and cap capacity checks occur after their owners allocated them; the borrowed checks cannot reserve these allocations retroactively.
The source derivation covers the pinned release x86_64 Linux configuration and dependencies. Allocation observations validate its limits and do not define them.
Complete simultaneous worker/coordinator lifetimes remain unfinished. Ordinary pool admission rejects the incomplete phase profile.

Isolated finalizer timings do not establish throughput or a performance gain. Nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
